dedupe_keys.name: dharanokxa gis to hydraulic water network design pipeline

description: DharaNokxa builds a candidate drinking-water distribution network from household locations and an elevated storage reservoir location. Its Python pipeline creates a road-like pipe topology, estimates demonstration demand and terrain, chooses HDPE pipe sizes, and runs EPANET 2.2 through WNTR. It then records pressure corrections, attempted downsizing, GIS outputs, model files and an engineering report. The README gives commands for a deterministic 100-household demonstration and for a local API and web interface. The repository is MIT-licensed, while EPANET, WNTR and other dependencies retain their own licences. The authors explicitly label the Assam/JJM profile and demand assumptions as provisional; generated designs require engineer review before field use. This review opened documentation and the file tree but did not run the model or inspect its output package. Geographic scope is determined by supplied household and reservoir points, with an Indian demonstration profile. A modeller could create alternative network layouts and compare pressure or demand-delivery scenarios. Related catalogue models model-epanet and model-wntr provide the hydraulic engines used here. The pipeline prepares a model; it is not a verified as-built water-system inventory. Coverage beyond the demonstration network has not been verified.
name: DharaNokxa GIS-to-hydraulic water-network design pipeline
